Chapter 7 — Measuring Progress: New Metrics for Innovation.
If you’ve ever worked in business, you know the usual scorecard—sales numbers, market share, maybe product usage stats. Sure, these numbers matter, but here’s a question to consider: are we really helping our customers make progress in their lives?
To get a real answer, organizations need a fresh approach to measuring success. It’s not just about what people buy, or how often they use a product. It’s about whether they’re actually moving forward—getting closer to their goals.
Let’s talk about some ways you can measure what really matters:
First, think about progress indicators. Instead of just tracking logins or transactions, ask yourself—are people completing the jobs they set out to do? Take a fitness app, for example. It’s not enough to count daily users. What if you could measure real improvements in someone’s health, or see how their confidence grows over time? That’s a much deeper kind of progress.
Next, pay attention to friction points. Where do customers struggle, get stuck, or even give up? Every one of these moments is like a flashing sign—an opportunity for you to step in, fix what’s broken, and make the experience smoother. That’s where innovation often starts.
And don’t forget about emotional resonance. How do people feel when they use your solution? Are they relieved, empowered, maybe reassured? Sometimes, the biggest impact is emotional. You can uncover this through simple surveys, honest interviews, or just observing what happens before, during, and after someone interacts with your product.
When you start focusing on these metrics, you’ll notice something interesting. You’ll see the gap between what you meant to deliver—and what customers actually experience. Imagine a home improvement store. Sales might be through the roof, but what if a lot of customers leave feeling overwhelmed by complex projects? That’s a signal. Maybe it’s time to offer hands-on workshops, or personalized guides that help people feel more confident tackling repairs.
These new ways of measuring progress aren’t just numbers—they help you make smarter choices. Instead of chasing every shiny new feature, your team can zero in on changes that truly move the needle for your customers.
So, the next time you’re looking at your results, ask yourself: are we just counting transactions—or are we really helping people move forward?
